firstParty.answer: Choose a first-party API when you need the newest vendor features and direct support. Choose a multi-model platform when unified access, provider fallback, or simpler model switching matters more.
firstParty.question: Should I use a first-party API or a multi-model API platform?

providerTypes.answer: A foundation model provider develops and serves its own models. A model service provider offers one API or platform that routes requests to models from multiple developers.
providerTypes.question: What is the difference between a foundation model provider and a model service provider?

selection.answer: Compare model availability, token pricing, context and output limits, rate limits, data handling, regional access, latency, reliability, SDK support, and production observability.
selection.question: What should I compare when choosing an LLM API provider?

guide.compareModels: Compare coding models side by side

modelAccess.description: Confirm that the provider carries the coding models, versions, context windows, and tool-calling features your application needs.
modelAccess.title: Model access

pricingLimits.description: Compare input and output token prices together with rate limits, regional availability, quotas, and any caching discounts.
pricingLimits.title: Pricing and limits

productionFit.description: Review privacy terms, data retention, reliability, latency, SDK quality, observability, and fallback options before production use.
productionFit.title: Production fit

guide.description: Start with the models your product requires, then compare their real delivery conditions. First-party providers offer direct access to their own models; model service providers can simplify access to multiple model families through one API.
